question: Why did one famous study put 47% of US jobs at high risk of automation, and an OECD study only about 9%?
answer: Because the first scored whole occupations, the second the tasks people actually do. Frey and Osborne rated an occupation at risk if its core tasks could be automated. The OECD team found that people in the same occupation do different mixes of tasks, many hard to automate. Machines take tasks; jobs are bundles of them.
move: Before trusting a big forecast, ask what exactly it counted.
ask: If machines took over a third of my tasks, which of the rest would I want to grow?
